== Overview ==

Result codes are UInt32 values used throughout [[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX|NEX]] to indicate the outcome of an operation. They are often represented using the [[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX/Types#Result|Result]] type. If the MSB is set, the result code indicates a error. Most results are used as errors. Some result codes are only triggered by the client, and are not sent from a server.

Result codes are structured as follows:

{| class="wikitable"
! Bits !! Description
|-
| 31 || Error flag. If set, the result indicates a error
|-
| 30-16 || Category
|-
| 15-0 || Code within the category
|}

== Known Result Codes ==

=== Core ===

These result codes are usually used only by the client, or are returned by the server to indicate generic errors.

{| class="wikitable"
! Value !! Name !! Description
|-
| <code>0x00010001</code> || <code>Core::Unknown</code> || An unknown error has occured. Also indicates a success when the error bit is not set
|-
| <code>0x00010002</code> || <code>Core::NotImplemented</code> || The called method does not exist on the receiver
|-
| <code>0x00010003</code> || <code>Core::InvalidPointer</code> || The operation specifies or accesses an invalid pointer
|-
| <code>0x00010004</code> || <code>Core::OperationAborted</code> || The operation was aborted, either intentionally or due to time out
|-
| <code>0x00010005</code> || <code>Core::Exception</code> || A generic exception was raised
|-
| <code>0x00010006</code> || <code>Core::AccessDenied</code> || An attempt was made to access data in an incorrect manner. This may be due to inadequate permission or the data, file, etc. not existing
|-
| <code>0x00010007</code> || <code>Core::InvalidHandle</code> || The operation specifies or accesses an invalid DOHandle
|-
| <code>0x00010008</code> || <code>Core::InvalidIndex</code> || The operation specifies or accesses an invalid index
|-
| <code>0x00010009</code> || <code>Core::OutOfMemory</code> || The system could not allocate or access enough memory or disk space to perform the specified operation
|-
| <code>0x0001000A</code> || <code>Core::InvalidArgument</code> || The operation parameters were not valid. This can mean parameters were out of range, were an invalid combination, etc.
|-
| <code>0x0001000B</code> || <code>Core::Timeout</code> || The operation did not complete within the specified timeout for that operation
|-
| <code>0x0001000C</code> || <code>Core::InitializationFailure</code> || Initialization of the component failed
|-
| <code>0x0001000D</code> || <code>Core::CallInitiationFailure</code> || The call failed to initialize
|-
| <code>0x0001000E</code> || <code>Core::RegistrationError</code> || An error occurred during registration
|-
| <code>0x0001000F</code> || <code>Core::BufferOverflow</code> || The buffer is too large to be handled
|-
| <code>0x00010010</code> || <code>Core::InvalidLockState</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x00010011</code> || <code>Core::InvalidSequence</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x00010012</code> || <code>Core::SystemError</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x00010013</code> || <code>Core::Cancelled</code> || Unknown
|}

=== RendezVous ===

Original/stock Rendez-Vous result codes. These could be seen in Rendez-Vous games acorss multiple protocols. Nintendo replaced many of these result codes with more specific result codes in NEX.

{| class="wikitable"
! Value !! Name !! Description
|-
| <code>0x00030001</code> || <code>RendezVous::ConnectionFailure</code> || Connection was unable to be established, either with the Rendez-Vous backend or a peer
|-
| <code>0x00030002</code> || <code>RendezVous::NotAuthenticated</code> || The Principal could not be authenticated by the Authentication Service
|-
| <code>0x00030064</code> || <code>RendezVous::InvalidUsername</code> || The Principal tried to log in with an invalid user name, i.e. the user name does not exist in the database
|-

|-

=== PythonCore ===

[[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX|NEX]]/Rendez-Vous were partially written in Python. These errors usually indicate that the recipient was able to parse the incoming data, but something has gone wrong with the type system. These errors are also common in pre-[[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX|NEX]]v2 titles as they tend to lack input validation.

{| class="wikitable"
! Value !! Name !! Description
|-
| <code>0x00040001</code> || <code>PythonCore::Exception</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x00040002</code> || <code>PythonCore::TypeError</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x00040003</code> || <code>PythonCore::IndexError</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x00040004</code> || <code>PythonCore::InvalidReference</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x00040005</code> || <code>PythonCore::CallFailure</code> || Unknown

|-
| <code>0x00040009</code> || <code>PythonCore::ConversionError</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x0004000A</code> || <code>PythonCore::ValidationError</code> || Unknown
|}

| <code>0x00690001</code> || <code>DataStore::Unknown</code> || An unknown error has occured. Also indicates a success when the error bit is not set
|-
| <code>0x00690002</code> || <code>DataStore::InvalidArgument</code> || The operation parameters were not valid. This can mean parameters were out of range, were an invalid combination, etc.
|-
| <code>0x00690003</code> || <code>DataStore::PermissionDenied</code> || The user did not have permission to perform the given operation. For example, trying to delete an object you do not have permission for
|-
| <code>0x00690004</code> || <code>DataStore::NotFound</code> || An invalid DataID was used
|-
| <code>0x00690005</code> || <code>DataStore::AlreadyLocked</code> || The object is inaccessible due to be locked
|-
| <code>0x00690006</code> || <code>DataStore::UnderReviewing</code> || The object is inaccessible due to being under review
|-
| <code>0x00690007</code> || <code>DataStore::Expired</code> || The object is inaccessible due to being expired
|-
| <code>0x00690008</code> || <code>DataStore::InvalidCheckToken</code> || <code>DataStoreNewArrivalCheckToken</code> is invalid
|-
| <code>0x00690009</code> || <code>DataStore::SystemFileError</code> || Unknown
|-
| <code>0x0069000A</code> || <code>DataStore::OverCapacity</code> || A batch operation list is over capacity
|-
| <code>0x0069000B</code> || <code>DataStore::OperationNotAllowed</code> || The attempted operation is not valid, but is not a permissions issue. For example, trying to self-rate an object that has self rating disabled
|-
| <code>0x0069000C</code> || <code>DataStore::InvalidPassword</code> || The provided password was incorrect
|-
| <code>0x0069000D</code> || <code>DataStore::ValueNotEqual</code> || The [[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX/Protocols/DataStoreProtocol#DataStoreChangeMetaCompareParam|DataStoreChangeMetaCompareParam]] check failed
|}
